71	/-! ## The Σ-extension as a presheaf on the big site -/
72	
73	/-- **The big-site carrier of the slice trick**: the Σ-extension of the type-valued
74	degree-zero Picard functor, `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)`.  Reducible so
75	that the stage-2 `sigmaExtension` calculus applies syntactically. -/
76	noncomputable abbrev pic0SigmaFunctor : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
77	  Over.sigmaExtension (Spec (.of k)) (pic0TypeFunctor C)

82	-- The amalgamation seams unify the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`
83	-- against the Σ-extension calculus by unfolding; within the DAT-2/PicEtMap 1600000
84	-- precedent.
85	/-- **The big-site Zariski sheaf certificate of the Σ-extension** (DAT-6 keystone,
86	worksheet §1.2 site gap 1): mathlib's reduction collapses the sheaf condition to
87	elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers, where the Σ-components glue by
88	`Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms` and the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation
89	bridge. -/
90	theorem pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf :
91	    Presieve.IsSheaf Scheme.zariskiTopology (pic0SigmaFunctor C) := by
92	  rw [Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange]
93	  intro Y S hS
94	  obtain ⟨𝓤, rfl⟩ := Scheme.exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology hS
95	  rw [Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff]
96	  intro x hx
97	  -- glue the Σ-components along the scheme-level cover
98	  have hpair : ∀ i j, pullback.fst (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x i).1
99	      = pullback.snd (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j) ≫ (x j).1 := fun i j =>
100	    congrArg Sigma.fst
101	      (hx i j (pullback (𝓤.f i) (𝓤.f j)) (pullback.fst _ _) (pullback.snd _ _)
102	        pullback.condition)
103	  obtain ⟨aY, ha⟩ : ∃ aY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k), ∀ i, 𝓤.f i ≫ aY = (x i).1 :=
104	    ⟨𝓤.glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair,
105	      fun i => 𝓤.ι_glueMorphisms (fun i => (x i).1) hpair i⟩
106	  -- the induced slice cover of `Over.mk aY` and its member sections
107	  haveI hop : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion
108	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left :=
109	    fun i => 𝓤.map_prop i
110	  have hcov : ∀ p : (Over.mk aY).left, ∃ i, p ∈ Scheme.Hom.opensRange
111	      ((Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)).left := by
112	    intro p
113	    obtain ⟨i, y, hy⟩ := 𝓤.exists_eq p
114	    exact ⟨i, y, hy⟩
115	  -- the fibre components are a compatible family on the slice cover
116	  have hcompat : ∀ (i j : 𝓤.I₀) (Z : Over (Spec (.of k)))
117	      (gi : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x i).1)) (gj : Z ⟶ Over.mk ((x j).1)),
118	      gi ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY)
119	          = gj ≫ (Over.homMk (𝓤.f j) (ha j) : Over.mk ((x j).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY) →
120	      pic0Map C gi ((x i).2) = pic0Map C gj ((x j).2) := by
121	    intro i j Z gi gj hg
122	    have hleft : gi.left ≫ 𝓤.f i = gj.left ≫ 𝓤.f j := congrArg Over.Hom.left hg
123	    have hdesc := Over.map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq gi gj
124	      (hx i j Z.left gi.left gj.left hleft)
125	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply, pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hdesc
126	  -- glue the fibre components by the stage-1 evaluation bridge
127	  obtain ⟨s, hs, hsu⟩ := pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover
128	    (fun i => (Over.homMk (𝓤.f i) (ha i) : Over.mk ((x i).1) ⟶ Over.mk aY))
129	    hcov (fun i => (x i).2) hcompat
130	  refine ⟨⟨aY, s⟩, fun i => ?_, ?_⟩
131	  · -- the glued Σ-element restricts to the members
132	    refine (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s ((x i).2)).mpr ?_
133	    rw [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply]
134	    exact hs i
135	  · -- uniqueness: Σ-components by `hom_ext`, fibres by bridge separation
136	    rintro ⟨a', s'⟩ ht'
137	    obtain rfl : aY = a' := 𝓤.hom_ext aY a' fun i =>
138	      (ha i).trans (congrArg Sigma.fst (ht' i) : 𝓤.f i ≫ a' = (x i).1).symm
139	    refine congrArg (Sigma.mk aY) (hsu s' fun i => ?_)
140	    have hmem := (Over.sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff (𝓤.f i) (ha i) s' ((x i).2)).mp
141	      (ht' i)
142	    rwa [pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply] at hmem

154	relatively representable open immersions into the Σ-extension sheaf (DAT-C's

132	/-- **The Abel morphism of a degree-zero class on the divisor scheme.**
133	
134	`divSchemeOver … : Over (Spec k)` is a test object of the degree-zero Picard functor, so a class
135	`lam : pic⁰(divSchemeOver …)` *is* a morphism to any representing object, by the universal
136	property.  No geometry is used: this is `rep.homEquiv.symm`.
137	
138	Every `JacobianData` producer of `Picard/JacobianDataAbelImage.lean` and
139	`Picard/JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean` takes such a morphism as an unproduced hypothesis `abel`.
140	Its `.left` (`abelOfPic0Class_left` below is `rfl`) is that hypothesis, so those producers are
141	reachable from a class. -/
142	def abelOfPic0Class {J : Over (Spec (.of k))}
143	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
144	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)) :
145	    divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J :=
146	  rep.homEquiv.symm lam
147	
148	/-- The underlying morphism of schemes out of `DivScheme g` — the `abel` of
149	`JacobianData.ofAbelImage`. -/
150	@[simp]
151	lemma abelOfPic0Class_left {J : Over (Spec (.of k))}
152	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
153	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)) :
154	    (abelOfPic0Class rep lam).left
155	      = ((rep.homEquiv.symm lam : divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ ⟶ J)).left :=
156	  rfl
157	
158	/-- **The compatibility square, proved rather than assumed.**
159	
160	The class of a composite `q ≫ abel` is the restriction `pic0Map C q lam` of `lam` along `q`.
161	This is `RepresentableBy.homEquiv_comp` after `Equiv.apply_symm_apply`, and it is what
162	`IsAbelClassifyCompatible` (`Picard/JacobianDataAbelSquare.lean:147`) posits for an abstractly
163	given `abel`.
164	
165	Recorded as the reason the "groups agree ≠ maps agree" gap (`I-0525`) does not arise here: the
166	gap is about relating two *independently named* morphisms, and this `abel` is named by the same
167	equivalence that names the classes. -/
168	lemma abelOfPic0Class_comp_class {J : Over (Spec (.of k))}
169	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
170	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂))
171	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂) :
172	    rep.homEquiv (q ≫ abelOfPic0Class rep lam) = pic0Map C q lam := by
173	  rw [abelOfPic0Class, rep.homEquiv_comp (f := q), Equiv.apply_symm_apply]
174	  rfl
175	
176	/-- **A field point whose class is pulled back from `lam` lifts through the Abel morphism.**
177	
178	If `q : overSpec k κ(y) ⟶ divSchemeOver …` carries `lam` to the class of the field point of `y`,
179	then `q ≫ abelOfPic0Class rep lam` **is** that field point — not merely a morphism with the same
180	class.  The upgrade is `Equiv.injective`: `homEquiv` is an equivalence, so two morphisms into `J`
181	with equal classes are equal.
182	
183	This is the step that would otherwise be the compatibility square. -/
184	lemma comp_abelOfPic0Class_eq_testPoint {J : Over (Spec (.of k))}
185	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
186	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)) (y : J.left)
187	    (q : overSpec k (Over.testPointField y) ⟶ divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂)
188	    (hq : pic0Map C q lam = rep.homEquiv (Over.testPoint y)) :
189	    q ≫ abelOfPic0Class rep lam = Over.testPoint y := by
190	  apply rep.homEquiv.injective
191	  rw [abelOfPic0Class_comp_class]
192	  exact hq
193	
194	/-- **The per-point residue-field lift, from the class statement.**
195	
196	`Over.testPoint y` has carrier `fromSpecResidueField y` by definition
197	(`Over.testPoint_left`), so the previous lemma delivers exactly the hypothesis
198	`surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift` (`Picard/JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean:82`) and
199	hence `JacobianData.ofAbelLifts` consume — with the morphism and the square supplied here
200	instead of assumed. -/
201	lemma residueField_lift_of_pic0_class {J : Over (Spec (.of k))}
202	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
203	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂))
204	    (hcl : ∀ y : J.left,
205	      ∃ q : overSpec k (Over.testPointField y) ⟶ divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂,
206	        pic0Map C q lam = rep.homEquiv (Over.testPoint y))
207	    (y : J.left) :
208	    ∃ q : Spec (J.left.residueField y) ⟶ DivScheme k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂,
209	      q ≫ (abelOfPic0Class rep lam).left = J.left.fromSpecResidueField y := by
210	  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := hcl y
211	  exact ⟨q.left, congrArg Over.Hom.left
212	    (comp_abelOfPic0Class_eq_testPoint rep lam y q hq)⟩
213	
214	/-- **DAT-J's `quasiCompact` field, from a class on the divisor scheme.**
215	
216	Given a representation `rep` of the degree-zero Picard functor by `J`, a degree-zero class `lam`
217	on `divSchemeOver …`, and the statement that *every* point of `J.left` has its class pulled back
218	from `lam` along some field point of the divisor scheme, the structure morphism `J.hom` is
219	quasi-compact.
220	
221	The chain: `hcl` gives per-point lifts through `abelOfPic0Class rep lam`
222	(`residueField_lift_of_pic0_class`), those give point surjectivity
223	(`surjective_of_forall_exists_residueField_lift`), `DivScheme g` is a compact space
224	(`compactSpace_divScheme`, DD-Q) and `Spec k` is affine, so DJ-0's
225	`quasiCompact_of_surjective` applies.
226	
227	**What is and is not discharged.**  `lam` and `hcl` are hypotheses; this proves the implication.
228	What it removes from the previous obligation list is the Abel *morphism* and the compatibility
229	*square* — neither is an input any more. -/
230	theorem quasiCompact_of_pic0_class_surjective {J : Over (Spec (.of k))}
231	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
232	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂))
233	    (hcl : ∀ y : J.left,
234	      ∃ q : overSpec k (Over.testPointField y) ⟶ divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂,
235	        pic0Map C q lam = rep.homEquiv (Over.testPoint y)) :
236	    QuasiCompact J.hom :=
237	  quasiCompact_of_forall_residueField_lift_from_divScheme A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ J
238	    (abelOfPic0Class rep lam).left (residueField_lift_of_pic0_class rep lam hcl)

240	/-! ### The `κ(y)` pin was never what `QuasiCompact` needed
241	
242	`hcl` above pins the lift's source to `overSpec k κ(y)`.  That pin is **not needed**: point
243	surjectivity only asks for *some* point of the divisor scheme lying over `y`, and the residue
244	field of the test that produces it is irrelevant.  So a divisor produced over a finite separable
245	*splitting field* `L` of `κ(y)` — which is what the effectivity chain
246	(`Picard/JacobianDataAbelEffectivePoint.lean`) actually delivers — is accepted as produced, with
247	no descent step.
248	
249	**SCOPED after a fresh-context audit (`I-1072`), because the first draft of this heading claimed
250	more than the theorem.**  It said the widening "deletes an obligation two files record as the
251	honest remaining cost".  It does not delete anything: the extension-tolerant hypothesis is
252	**equivalent** to bare `Function.Surjective (abelOfPic0Class rep lam).left.base`, not weaker
253	than it (converse: pick `x` in the fibre over `y`, take `T := overSpec k κ(x)` with `q :=
254	Over.testPoint x`).  Since `quasiCompact_of_surjective_from_divScheme` already consumed bare
255	surjectivity, DJ-0 was never asking for the pin in the first place.
256	
257	What survives, and it is a characterisation rather than a discount: the `Spec κ(y)` pin in
258	`JacobianData.ofAbelLifts`'s `hlift` (`Picard/JacobianDataAbelSurj.lean:153`) is an artefact of
259	that signature, not a requirement of quasi-compactness.  A lane reading those two files' "what
260	remains is DESCENT" should check whether its consumer is the qc field — for that consumer there
261	is nothing to descend — and any *other* consumer of the `hlift` signature still owes it. -/
262	
263	/-- **The extension-tolerant lift hypothesis gives point surjectivity.**
264	
265	For each `y`, a `k`-test `T` with a point, a morphism `e : T ⟶ overSpec k κ(y)`, and a
266	divisor-scheme morphism `q` whose class matches that of `e ≫ Over.testPoint y`.  For a field
267	extension `L ⊇ κ(y)` this is `T := overSpec k L`, so the splitting field the effectivity chain
268	lands over is accepted directly.
269	
270	Strictly weaker than `hcl`: `extensionTolerant_of_kappaPinned` below is the `T := overSpec k κ(y)`,
271	`e := 𝟙` face. -/
272	theorem surjective_of_extensionTolerant_lift {J : Over (Spec (.of k))}
273	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
274	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂))
275	    (h : ∀ y : J.left, ∃ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (_ : Nonempty T.left)
276	      (e : T ⟶ overSpec k (Over.testPointField y))
277	      (q : T ⟶ divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂),
278	      pic0Map C q lam = rep.homEquiv (e ≫ Over.testPoint y)) :
279	    Function.Surjective (abelOfPic0Class rep lam).left.base := by
280	  intro y
281	  obtain ⟨T, ⟨p⟩, e, q, hq⟩ := h y
282	  have hqt : q ≫ abelOfPic0Class rep lam = e ≫ Over.testPoint y := by
283	    apply rep.homEquiv.injective
284	    rw [abelOfPic0Class_comp_class]
285	    exact hq
286	  refine ⟨q.left.base p, ?_⟩
287	  have h2 := congrArg (fun (m : T ⟶ J) => m.left.base p) hqt
288	  refine h2.trans ?_
289	  exact Over.testPoint_base y (e.left.base p)
290	
291	/-- **The qc field from the extension-tolerant hypothesis** — the form to hand a producer,
292	since it accepts a divisor produced over any extension of the residue field. -/
293	theorem quasiCompact_of_extensionTolerant_lift {J : Over (Spec (.of k))}
294	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
295	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂))
296	    (h : ∀ y : J.left, ∃ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (_ : Nonempty T.left)
297	      (e : T ⟶ overSpec k (Over.testPointField y))
298	      (q : T ⟶ divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂),
299	      pic0Map C q lam = rep.homEquiv (e ≫ Over.testPoint y)) :
300	    QuasiCompact J.hom :=
301	  quasiCompact_of_surjective_from_divScheme A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂ J
302	    (abelOfPic0Class rep lam).left (surjective_of_extensionTolerant_lift rep lam h)
303	
304	/-- The `κ(y)`-pinned hypothesis is the `T := overSpec k κ(y)`, `e := 𝟙` face of the
305	extension-tolerant one — recorded so the generalisation is visibly not a weakening of the
306	*conclusion*, only of the hypothesis. -/
307	theorem extensionTolerant_of_kappaPinned {J : Over (Spec (.of k))}
308	    (rep : (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J)
309	    (lam : pic0Subgroup C (divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂))
310	    (hcl : ∀ y : J.left,
311	      ∃ q : overSpec k (Over.testPointField y) ⟶ divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂,
312	        pic0Map C q lam = rep.homEquiv (Over.testPoint y)) (y : J.left) :
313	    ∃ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) (_ : Nonempty T.left)
314	      (e : T ⟶ overSpec k (Over.testPointField y))
315	      (q : T ⟶ divSchemeOver k A B g r₁ r₂ b₁ b₂),
316	      pic0Map C q lam = rep.homEquiv (e ≫ Over.testPoint y) := by
317	  obtain ⟨q, hq⟩ := hcl y
318	  refine ⟨overSpec k (Over.testPointField y), ⟨Nonempty.some inferInstance⟩, 𝟙 _, q, ?_⟩
319	  rw [Category.id_comp]

161	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
162	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] {n : ℕ}

168	variable (C π n) in
169	/-- **The Abel transformation into the degree-zero Picard functor**: under the chart-index
170	degree constraint `deg Z = m·d₁ − n`, the chart value of `DivSchemeAbel.lean` — the Abel class
171	of the divisor family, shifted by the Σ-family of `Z` and by `m` inverse powers of the pinned
172	θ-family — is a natural transformation `divFunctor C π n ⟶ pic0TypeFunctor C`.
173	
174	The degree ledger of `degAt_chartValue` is what makes the target the degree-*zero* functor:
175	the three factors contribute `n`, `deg Z` and `−m·d₁`, which the constraint sums to zero. -/
176	def chartValueTrans (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
177	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
178	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (n : ℤ)) :
179	    divFunctor C π n ⟶ pic0TypeFunctor C where
180	  app T := TypeCat.ofHom fun s => ⟨chartValue C π n m Z T.unop s,
181	    chartValue_mem_pic0Subgroup C π n m Z hdeg T.unop s⟩
182	  naturality T T' g := by
183	    refine ConcreteCategory.hom_ext _ _ fun s => ?_
184	    exact Subtype.ext ((picEtMap_chartValue C π n m Z g.unop s).symm)
185

/-!
# The big-site Zariski sheaf `pic⁰` and the 01JJ seam (DAT-6, stage 3)

The slice trick assembled: the Σ-extension of the degree-zero Picard functor is an
honest sheaf for the big Zariski topology on `Scheme`, and mathlib's 01JJ
local-representability engine applied to it descends to a representation of the
degree-zero Picard functor itself on the slice.

* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0TypeFunctor C`: the degree-zero Picard functor with values in
  types — the `forget₂ ⋙ forget` massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once
  (`pic0TypeFunctor_obj`/`pic0TypeFunctor_map_apply` are `rfl`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor C : Scheme.{u}ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u`: the Σ-extension
  `T ↦ Σ (a : T ⟶ Spec k), pic⁰(Over.mk a)` — the big-site carrier.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0SigmaFunctor_isSheaf` / **`pic0SigmaSheaf C`**: the sheaf
  certificate.  By mathlib's own reduction the big-site sheaf condition collapses to
  elementwise ∃!-amalgamation on honest open covers
  (`Precoverage.isSheaf_toGrothendieck_iff_of_isStableUnderBaseChange`,
  `exists_cover_of_mem_pretopology`, `Presieve.isSheafFor_arrows_iff` — the
  `BigZariski` TODO is never touched): the Σ-components glue by
  `Scheme.Cover.glueMorphisms`, the fibre components glue by the DAT-6 stage-1
  evaluation bridge (`pic0Subgroup_existsUnique_of_cover`), and the two layers are
  stitched by the stage-2 amalgamation seam (`sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff`) and
  compatibility descent (`map_eq_of_sigmaExtension_map_eq`).
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfCharts`: **the DAT-glue seam** — given a
  chart family of relatively representable open immersions into `pic0SigmaSheaf`
  (DAT-C) that is jointly locally surjective (DAT-B), mathlib's
  `Scheme.LocalRepresentability.representableBy` produces a representation of the
  Σ-extension by the glued scheme, and the stage-2 Σ-descent `overSlice` turns it
  into a representation of `pic0TypeFunctor C` by the glued scheme over the
  Σ-component of the universal element.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

/-! ## The type-valued degree-zero Picard functor -/

/-- The degree-zero Picard functor with values in types: the `forget₂ ⋙ forget`
massage of `pic0Functor`, owned here once for the Σ-extension statements. -/
noncomputable abbrev pic0TypeFunctor : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u :=
  (pic0Functor C ⋙ forget₂ CommGrpCat GrpCat) ⋙ forget GrpCat

import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.QuasiCompact
import Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Morphisms.UnderlyingMap

/-!
# DJ-0: quasi-compactness from a compact-space source via a surjection

The smallest, ungated brick of the DAT-J worksheet (`informal/w4-datj-worksheet.md`
§2.4): the abstract topological shape that `JacobianData.quasiCompact` consumes to get
quasi-compactness of the Jacobian structure morphism from the Abel image of `Div^g`-lite.

The mathematics is entirely mathlib's: the continuous surjective image of a compact space
is compact (`Function.Surjective.compactSpace`). This file packages that for scheme
morphisms and adds the quasi-compactness corollary over an affine base, so DAT-J's qc
field is a one-line instantiation. It is deliberately **Challenge-free** (mathlib-only, no
curve/Challenge imports) — the DAT-J producer cone must not cycle through `Challenge.lean`
(worksheet §0.5 / risk 1).

## Main results

* `AlgebraicGeometry.compactSpace_of_surjective`: if `f : X ⟶ Y` is a surjection of
  schemes out of a compact-space source `X`, then `Y` is a compact space.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.quasiCompact_of_surjective`: a structure morphism `g : Y ⟶ Z` to an
  affine base is quasi-compact as soon as `Y` receives such a surjection. This is the
  shape DAT-J's DJ-1 consumes with `X := Div^g` (`compactSpace_divScheme`), `f := abel`
  the Abel morphism, `g := J.hom`, `Z := Spec k`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

variable {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}

/-- **DJ-0, compact-image half.** If `f : X ⟶ Y` is a surjection of schemes out of a
compact-space source, then the target is a compact space: the underlying map of `f` is a
continuous surjection (`Scheme.Hom.continuous`), and the continuous surjective image of a
compact space is compact (`Function.Surjective.compactSpace`). -/
theorem compactSpace_of_surjective (f : X ⟶ Y) [CompactSpace X]
    (hf : Function.Surjective f.base) : CompactSpace Y :=
  hf.compactSpace f.continuous

/-- **DJ-0, quasi-compactness corollary.** A structure morphism `g : Y ⟶ Z` to an affine
base is quasi-compact as soon as `Y` receives a surjection `f : X ⟶ Y` from a
compact-space source `X`. Over an affine base, `QuasiCompact g` is exactly `CompactSpace Y`
(`HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine`, the `DivSchemeQProj` pattern), which the
compact-image half supplies.

This is the abstract shape `JacobianData.quasiCompact` consumes: instantiate
`X := Div^g` (compact via `compactSpace_divScheme`), `f := abel` the Abel morphism
(surjective on points, DJ-1), `g := J.hom`, `Z := Spec k`. -/
theorem quasiCompact_of_surjective (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z) [IsAffine Z]
    [CompactSpace X] (hf : Function.Surjective f.base) : QuasiCompact g :=
  haveI : CompactSpace Y := compactSpace_of_surjective f hf
  HasAffineProperty.iff_of_isAffine.mpr ‹_›

end AlgebraicGeometry

/-- **The degree-zero subgroup** of the étale Picard group of a test object: the
classes of degree zero at every field point of the test.  The object part of the
degree-zero Picard functor `pic0Functor` (gap G-D7). -/
def pic0Subgroup (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) : Subgroup (picEt C T) where
  carrier := {lam | ∀ (K : Type u) [Field K] [Algebra k K] (t : overSpec k K ⟶ T),

  one_mem' := by

    exact degAt_one t
  mul_mem' := by

    rw [degAt_mul, ha K t, hb K t, add_zero]
  inv_mem' := by

    rw [degAt_inv, ha K t, neg_zero]

Σ-element iff the fibre component of the source restricts to the prescribed fibre
component along the canonical slice morphism over the prescribed structure
morphism. -/
lemma sigmaExtension_map_mk_eq_iff {T' T : C} (g : T' ⟶ T) {a : T ⟶ S} {b : T' ⟶ S}
    (w : g ≫ a = b) (s : F.obj (op (Over.mk a))) (y : F.obj (op (Over.mk b))) :
    (sigmaExtension S F).map g.op ⟨a, s⟩ = ⟨b, y⟩
      ↔ F.map (Over.homMk g (show g ≫ (Over.mk a).hom = (Over.mk b).hom from w) :

  rw [sigmaExtension_map_mk]
  constructor
  · intro h
    have h2 := sigmaExtension_snd_eq F rfl h
    rw [mkCongr_rfl, op_id, F.map_id] at h2
    exact h2.symm
  · intro h

Over.mk a`, evaluated at a Σ-element over `a`: the structure morphism is `Z.hom` and
the fibre component is the honest slice restriction `F.map g.op`. -/
